jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in Nutrition and Inflammatory Bowel Disease
jobs.description:
The National Center of Excellence for the Molecular Prediction of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (PREDICT), based at Department of Clinical Medicine, Aalborg University (AAU) in Copenhagen, is looking to recruit a highly skilled and motivated PhD student in nutrition and inflammatory bowel disease to join our international and interdisciplinary group of dedicated researchers.The 3-year stipend (full-time, 37 hours per week) is available within the doctoral program Clinical Science, Laboratory and Translational Medicine, and is open for appointment from 1st of March 2027 or soon thereafter.

**Your work tasks
**We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to join our Nutrition Research Group and contribute to research exploring the role of diet in the development and progression of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The project aims to improve our understanding of diet-disease relationships and generate evidence that can support future dietary recommendations for individuals living with IBD.

The PhD student will work with large population-based cohorts to investigate associations between dietary patterns, nutritional exposures, and disease outcomes. As part of an interdisciplinary research environment, you will collaborate closely with epidemiologists, nutrition scientists, clinicians, and biostatisticians engaged in internationally recognized research.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Conducting systematic literature reviews and evidence syntheses

• 
Developing research protocols and statistical analysis plans

• 
Managing and analyzing large-scale epidemiological data

• 
Conducting statistical analyses using R and other relevant software

• 
Writing and publishing scientific articles in peer-reviewed journals

• 
Presenting research findings at national and international conferences

• 
Contributing to collaborative research activities within the Center and with external partners

You will receive supervision and training from experienced researchers and become an integral part of a dynamic and supportive research environment.

Your competencies We are looking for an ambitious and self-driven candidate with a strong interest in nutrition, epidemiology, and inflammatory bowel disease research. Previous experience in nutrition-related research, preferably in the field of inflammatory bowel disease, is an advantage.

The ideal candidate has:

• 
A Master's degree in Nutrition and Dietetics, Human Nutrition, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Sciences, or another relevant discipline

• 
Knowledge of nutritional epidemiology and inflammatory bowel disease

• 
Experience writing scientific reports, theses, or manuscripts

• 
Familiarity with statistical programming, preferably in R

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• 
Excellent collaboration and communication skills

• 
Excellent written and spoken English proficiency

• 
The ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary research team

**Qualification requirements
**PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School in Medicine, Biomedical Science and Technology in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions.

According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Please visit the website of the doctoral school for further information on admission requirements.

Who we are
PREDICT is at the forefront of international research to unravel the cause and prognosis of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), which are chronic and disabling conditions affecting millions of people worldwide. The Center is composed of biologists, clinicians, epidemiologists, and data scientists working with collaborators nationally and internationally to push the boundaries of precision medicine research and create real-world impact in IBD. We have state-of-the-art facilities within the center and this means through PREDICT you will be part of a well-funded research environment equipped with the latest technologies, unique data, and a world-leading network of collaborators.

We offer an exciting PhD program in a dynamic, high-performing, international environment with dedicated, friendly colleagues. We also offer superb opportunities for personal and professional development and unique access to state-of-the-art data resources, including linkable Danish nationwide health registries, Danish National Biobank data and individual level clinical data from the largest Danish IBD inception cohort; the NorDIBD Cohort.

You can read more about PREDICT here.

**About the Department of Clinical Medicine
**The Department of Clinical Medicine provides research-based teaching across all disciplines of the medical degree programme and conducts research within the clinical specialties.

Read more about the Department of Clinical Medicine here.

**How to apply
**Your application must include the following:

• 
Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• 
Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• 
Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• 
Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?     If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School in Medicine, Biomedical Science and Technology

**Salary and terms of employment
**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Principal Scientist - Analytical Development, Synthetics
jobs.description:
About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Principal Scientist, Analytical Development, you'll use your extensive experience in the analysis of synthetic therapeutics, including peptides and oligonucleotides, to serve as the analytical lead supporting our synthetics programs from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

You will support both early- and late-stage development, including phase-appropriate method validations and Quality Control activities, setting and justifying specifications, process and product characterization, and preparation of CMC regulatory submissions, including NDAs and MAAs. You will drive analytical strategies and manage analytical activities across multiple CROs and CDMOs, helping to ensure smooth progression from clinical manufacturing to commercial readiness.

What you'll do

• Own analytical strategy for synthetics programs, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, from first-in-human through commercial readiness.

• Establish phase-appropriate analytical approaches, including setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, reference standards, stability protocols, comparability assessments and risk assessments.

• Provide technical input to CDMOs on method development and validation (especially for purity methods), as well as product characterization.

• Manage analytical method transfer, optimization and validation with external partners, including in support of commercial readiness.

• If appropriate, ensure an appropriate mechanism of action-based potency assay is in place to support Phase 3 readiness.

• Provide analytical expertise on CMC sub-teams, working closely with Drug Substance, Drug Product, Research, Quality and Regulatory colleagues.

• Provide analytical support for process characterization, including determination of Critical Quality Attributes and appropriate validation of methods for testing In-Process Controls.

• Lead and manage analytical CROs/CDMOs, material suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators; monitor regulatory trends, integrate new analytical approaches, identify opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs, and advise colleagues on data interpretation.

• Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions, from first-in-human through NDAs and MAAs, and represent Hemab as an analytical expert in regulatory interactions when needed.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Proven industry experience setting analytical strategy for synthetic therapeutics, particularly peptides and oligonucleotides, with substantial exposure to late-stage development through commercialization.

• Strong working knowledge of phase-appropriate analytical method development and validations, setting and justifying specifications, product characterization, impurity marker synthesis and qualification, comparability assessments and regulatory submissions, especially NDAs/MAAs supporting late-stage synthetic programs.

• Significant experience managing CROs/CDMOs, including navigating technical problems where an external partner needs hands-on guidance.

• Strong understanding of ICH expectations for stability and method validation, together with experience producing analytical content for regulatory submissions.

• Flexibility, a proactive approach and comfort operating in a fast-paced biotech environment spanning multiple time zones.

• A relevant scientific degree, with a PhD preferred, and the technical depth to operate as an independent analytical expert.

Nice to have

• Experience with mechanism of action-based potency assays.

• Experience establishing reference standards.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. You will likely build some of your own tools and processes instead of inheriting finished products. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This position spans early- and late-stage development and works across multiple internal teams, CROs, CDMOs, suppliers, consultants, vendors and collaborators. Hemab operates across multiple time zones.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Please answer in your application:

Have you managed external CDMOs delivering analytical testing for synthetic drugs?

jobs.occupation: RF Engineer - Aalborg
jobs.description:
We are seeking an early-career RF Engineer to contribute to the design, development and validation of RF communication subsystems for nanosatellite missions.

In this role, you will support RF analysis and integration activities across UHF, VHF, S-band and X-band systems, perform link-budget analyses and help validate performance through hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.

You will join our Satellite Systems Hardware team in Aalborg and collaborate closely with colleagues across RF, Hardware, and Systems Engineering. You will work with GomSpace’s flight-proven NanoCom radios and SDR platform and gain practical experience across simulation, laboratory testing and system-level integration. Depending on the mission, you may contribute to conventional communication subsystems, software-defined radio applications or advanced RF sensing payloads.

Your Role

As RF Engineer, you will support the development and validation of RF subsystems for satellite missions, from link-budget analysis and RF-chain modelling through integration, hardware-in-the-loop testing and over-the-air validation.

Working with experienced engineers, you will gradually build the knowledge and practical experience needed to take responsibility for increasingly complex RF engineering tasks.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Support RF subsystem analysis and technical trade-offs across frequency bands, performance and mission constraints.

• Perform link-budget analysis and RF-chain modelling.

• Contribute to the definition and documentation of RF subsystem requirements and interfaces.

• Support the integration, verification and validation of RF subsystems, including hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.

• Assist with the evaluation and selection of RF front-end components across UHF, VHF, S-band and X-band.

• Prepare and carry out laboratory measurements using RF test equipment.

• Analyse test results and contribute to troubleshooting RF performance issues.

• Contribute to onboard signal-processing and data-reduction activities for RF applications.

• Document analyses, test activities and technical conclusions clearly and systematically.

• Provide technical input to mission proposals with support from experienced colleagues.

What Success Looks Like

In the initial phase, success means:

• Understanding GomSpace’s NanoCom product portfolio and SDR architecture.

• Building effective working relationships with colleagues across RF, Hardware and Systems Engineering.

• Completing a link-budget analysis for an active mission with guidance from experienced colleagues.

• Performing your first hardware-in-the-loop or over-the-air RF test using GomSpace equipment.

• Documenting your analysis and test results in a clear and structured way.

• Communicating RF results and technical observations clearly to colleagues from other disciplines.

Over time, you will take increasing responsibility for RF subsystem analysis, integration and verification activities. You will contribute independently to mission proposals and projects while helping develop reusable RF models, test methods and engineering tools.

What You Bring

You are a recent graduate or early-career RF engineer who is motivated to apply your technical knowledge to real satellite systems. You enjoy combining analytical work with practical laboratory activities and want to develop your skills within an experienced multidisciplinary team.

You likely bring:

• An MSc in Electrical Engineering, RF or Microwave Engineering, Telecommunications or a related field.

• Up to one year of relevant experience in RF engineering, communication systems, testing or integration.

• A basic understanding of RF engineering principles and communication systems.

• Experience with RF analysis, simulation or laboratory measurements gained through your studies, thesis, student employment, internship or first professional role.

• Familiarity with RF simulation or engineering tools such as CST, ADS, HFSS, MATLAB, Python or similar.

• Some experience with RF test equipment, such as spectrum analysers, vector network analysers or signal generators.

• An interest in satellite communication systems, software-defined radio or digital signal processing.

• Good analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Good written and spoken English.

Experience from the space or aerospace industry is an advantage but is not required. Relevant academic projects, thesis work, internships and student positions will also be considered.

Knowledge of modulation schemes, communication protocols, RF payloads, ECSS standards or space-grade RF qualification would be beneficial.

Who You Are

You are curious, systematic and motivated by the opportunity to turn engineering analysis into working hardware. You enjoy learning from experienced colleagues while also taking responsibility for your own tasks and development.

You are known for:

• Technical curiosity – eager to understand how RF systems perform in practice.

• Attention to detail – careful when analysing results, conducting tests and documenting conclusions.

• Hands-on problem solving – interested in moving between simulation tools and the laboratory bench.

• Collaborative communication – comfortable working with RF, systems, payload and hardware engineers.

• Structured execution – able to plan your work, follow up on tasks and communicate when support is needed.

• Customer focus – understanding that good engineering contributes directly to the success of our customers’ missions.

• Willingness to grow – open to feedback and motivated to build deeper RF subsystem expertise.

Why Join Us

You will have the opportunity to begin or develop your RF engineering career by working on communication systems for real nanosatellite missions.

The position offers hands-on experience across RF analysis, laboratory testing and system-level integration. You will work with flight-proven NanoCom radios and SDR platforms while learning from experienced specialists across RF, Hardware, and Systems Engineering.

Your work will contribute to mission proposals, subsystem development and technologies that ultimately fly in space. As your experience develops, you will take on increasing technical responsibility and have the opportunity to shape the tools and methods used by the team.

Join our mission

You are welcome to send your application in English. Interviews will be conducted on a continuous basis.

If you have any questions regarding the position, do not hesitate to contact Kelly Antonini, Systems Engineering and Hardware Manager: klan@gomspace.com.

The primary workplace will be at our premises in Aalborg, Denmark. The position involves laboratory, integration and test activities and therefore requires regular on-site presence. Salary and start date will be individually negotiated.

As part of our recruitment process, employment requires you to complete a background check conducted by an authorised third-party provider in accordance with applicable legislation.

We kindly draw your attention to the fact that we do not receive applications and CVs via email or by personal appearance. This is to protect and show consideration for your personal information. Apply for the job by following the application link below.

About GomSpace

GomSpace is a globally leading designer, integrator and manufacturer of high-end nano and microsatellites for customers in the academic, government and commercial markets. Our positions of strength include systems integration, small satellite subsystems and advanced miniaturized radio technology. At the core of our mission are our core values: Be helpful, communicate openly and frequently, and show true leadership.

Our international team is devoted to understanding our customers’ requirements and delivering high quality. We are listed in Stockholm (GOMX), headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in Sweden, Singapore, France, North America and Luxembourg. We have more than 300 employees servicing customers in more than 60 countries.

Aarhus University, Denmark

The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for two positions at the rank of:

•   Tenure Track Assistant Professor, or

•   Associate Professor

The positions are offered within the broad field of Materials Engineering and Manufacturing, with a particular focus on participating in the department’s research and education in materials engineering, durability, emerging and advanced materials, advanced manufacturing and surface engineering. The department seeks candidates who will help shape a modern materials science profile, in research as well as in teaching, and who have demonstrated relevant experience in the field.

Expected start date

July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

Research Areas

We welcome applicants with a solid background in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, materials-focused chemical engineering, applied physics, or closely related disciplines.

We particularly encourage applications within, but not limited to, the following research themes:

Additive and hybrid manufacturing

Including metal additive manufacturing, laser-based processing and welding, joining of metallic and dissimilar materials, post-processing, surface engineering, and process characterisation and modelling.

Materials durability and advanced materials

Including materials under demanding and extreme conditions, 4D printing, bioprinting, and biofabrication, surface modification, lubrication technologies and functional surfaces.

Applicants are expected to contribute to both fundamental understanding and applied solutions, with relevance to engineering systems and industrial applications

Research and Teaching Responsibilities

The selected candidates will:

•   Teach, contribute to, and develop courses in materials science and engineering, additive manufacturing, and manufacturing processes at different levels, from foundational bachelor’s courses to specialized master’s and PhD courses

•   Contribute directly to the further development of the materials and manufacturing science curriculum at different program levels

•   Supervise bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students

•   Attract external research funding

•   Engage in knowledge exchange with industry and research partners

•   Participate in departmental and university service activities

Your Profile

We are looking for candidates who can contribute to research, education, and innovation at an international level.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:

-   A PhD in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field

-   Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in materials science and engineering, with publications in leading international journals that match career stage

-   Experience in at least one of the research areas listed above, along with familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research methods

-   Interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry

-   For the positions as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:

-   Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing materials science courses, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study

-   For associate professor applicants: a documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level

Who we are

The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The  Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering  within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer

The department offers:

-   research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

-   an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

-   a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

-   a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

-   a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information

For more information about the position contact Head of Section of Manufacturing and Mechatronics, Professor Ramin Aghababaei (ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 9350 8956)

or Head of Section of Mechanics and Materials, Professor Michal Kazimierz Budzik (mibu@mpe.au.dk, +45 4189 3217)

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than December 8th, 2026.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track

Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship.

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level

• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists

• to create transparency in the academic career path

As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure

• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training

• a mentoring programme

• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level

As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The area performs analytical testing of raw materials, intermediates, finished products, process development samples, stability samples and control cells for extraneous agents. Techniques include physico-chemical testing, ELISA, HPLC and hemadsorption assays. Biochemistry also performs method development, validation and comparability testing.

You will join a QC department of approximately 90 employees across six teams. Our Core Leadership Team of Senior Managers works closely with First-Line Managers, the Operational Excellence Partner and a Quality Integrator to develop people and processes and maintain strong quality oversight.

jobs.occupation: Senior Scientist, Downstream, Late-Stage Process Development
jobs.description:
Join a fast-paced process development team where scientific expertise, collaboration and practical problem-solving help advance projects. As Senior Scientist, you will lead downstream development activities for mammalian cell culture processes, supporting their progression through late-stage development.

You will work closely with clients, laboratory technicians and colleagues across upstream, downstream and analytical disciplines. The role combines scientific leadership, study design, data interpretation and technical writing. Most hands-on laboratory work will be performed by technicians; you will work closely with them to develop protocols, design experiments and guide execution, ensuring studies are scientifically sound and generate decision-quality data.

**A role with scientific ownership and real project impact

**As a Senior Scientist, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of downstream development activities and contribute directly to the progression of projects. You will combine your scientific expertise with practical problem-solving and collaborate with both internal colleagues and clients.

The role gives you exposure to different projects, technologies and challenges rather than focusing on one narrow area. You will be involved in shaping studies, interpreting data and turning scientific findings into clear recommendations that support project decisions.

Your work will also give you the opportunity to collaborate closely with laboratory technicians and scientists, allowing you to stay connected to the practical side of process development while taking a leading role in the scientific direction.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Lead and coordinate downstream development activities for assigned projects, working with clients and cross-functional teams to align on project needs and deliver outcomes.

• Plan and evaluate downstream processes, including chromatography using ÄKTA systems and filtration operations such as depth filtration, virus filtration and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).

• Design studies and author practical protocols in close collaboration with laboratory technicians; provide scientific guidance during experimental execution.

• Interpret study results, apply appropriate statistical approaches—including design of experiments (DoE) where relevant—and communicate findings through clear presentations and reports.

• Contribute to process characterization, including failure mode and risk assessments such as FMEA, and author process characterization (PC) work reports.

• Support investigations and deviation handling by assessing technical causes, interpreting relevant data, and documenting conclusions and follow-up actions.

• Provide scientific and technical input to business activities and support the generation of information for regulatory submissions.

**Required Qualifications And Experience

**

• Education: Master’s or PhD in Biochemistry, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Process Technology, or a related discipline.

• Industrial experience: 5+ years with a Master’s degree, or 2+ years with a PhD.

• Downstream development: Demonstrated experience with mammalian cell culture processes.

• Unit operations: Chromatography and filtration; ideally ÄKTA systems and TFF systems.

• Study execution and data: Ability to plan, analyze and report complex development studies, including statistical analysis.

• Project work: Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities with scientific rigour and attention to detail.

• Communication: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to explain technical findings clearly to clients and colleagues.

• Language: Fluent written and spoken English.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience

**

• Process Characterization and FMEA

• Viral clearance studies or activities.

• Commercial manufacturing requirements and biologics regulatory frameworks, including relevant ICH guidelines and BLA submission requirements.

• Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DoE), including experimental design, data analysis, and evaluation using SAS JMP

• Liquid-handling automation, such as Tecan systems.

**What Will Help You Succeed

**You take ownership, bring a practical can-do attitude and are comfortable working at pace. You collaborate closely with technicians and colleagues, communicate openly, and use data and sound scientific judgement to find a way forward as project needs and priorities evolve.

**What You Can Expect From Us

**We want you to have the opportunity to use your scientific expertise while continuing to develop professionally. In this role, you can expect:

• Scientific ownership: Take responsibility for development activities and influence how studies are designed and executed.

• Variety: Work across different projects, technologies and scientific challenges rather than doing the same thing every day.

• Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with scientists, technicians, upstream and analytical colleagues as well as clients.

• Client exposure: Develop your ability to communicate scientific findings and recommendations directly with clients and contribute to project discussions.

• Professional development: Continue developing your expertise in downstream processing, process characterization, data analysis and late-stage development.

• Impact: See how your scientific work contributes to advancing biopharmaceutical processes towards later-stage development and manufacturing.

**A team where science and collaboration go hand in hand

**You will become part of a team where scientific knowledge, practical experience and collaboration are important to how we work. We value people who share knowledge, ask questions and are willing to challenge and support each other.

You will work closely with experienced colleagues across different disciplines, giving you the opportunity to learn from others while also bringing your own expertise to the team.

We believe that good science is strengthened by open communication, different perspectives and a willingness to find solutions together.

**Ready to make your next move?

**If you are looking for a role where you can combine scientific expertise, project ownership, client interaction and practical problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.

Apply through the AGC Biologics career site by **31 October 2026.

**Please note that we only accept applications through our recruitment system and cannot accept CVs by email.

**The Recruitment Process Will Include

**

• An initial screening interview with People & Culture

• An interview with the Hiring Manager

• A final interview, including a cognitive assessment and personality assessment

• A meet and greet with team members and a laboratory tour

• Reference checks

Applications will be reviewed on a continuous basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We may close the position before the application deadline once the right candidate has been identified.

_Location: We can only consider candidates currently based in Denmark or the Greater Malmö area, as relocation support is not available for this position.

_At AGC Biologics, we are committed to a fair and unbiased recruitment process. We assess candidates based on their skills, experience, qualifications, and potential to succeed in the role.

To support an objective recruitment process, please do not include a photo in your application or CV.

**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.
